Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১) Human vision is......?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
Humans have binocular vision, meaning both eyes work together to produce a single visual image. This provides depth perception (stereopsis) and a wider field of vision.

  • Binocular vision → Two eyes contribute to a single visual perception.

  • Uniocular/monocular vision → Vision using one eye.

Exam pearl:
Human vision = Binocular vision.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ২) Vestibular apparatus is the part of......?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The vestibular apparatus is located in the inner ear and is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation.

It consists of:

  • Semicircular canals → detect angular/rotational acceleration

  • Utricle and saccule → detect linear acceleration and head position

Exam pearl:
Vestibular apparatus → Inner ear → Balance.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ৩) A simple reflex arc includes how many components ?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
A simple reflex arc has 5 basic components:

  1. Receptor → detects the stimulus

  2. Sensory (afferent) neuron → carries impulse to CNS

  3. Integration center/interneuron → processes the impulse in CNS

  4. Motor (efferent) neuron → carries impulse to effector

  5. Effector → produces the response

Exam pearl:
Simple reflex arc = Receptor + Sensory neuron + Integration center + Motor neuron + Effector = 5 components.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ৪) Which is not a component of visual pathway?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The visual pathway includes:

Retina → Optic nerve → Optic chiasma → Optic tract → Lateral geniculate body (LGB) → Optic radiation → Visual cortex

  • Optic radiation → Part of visual pathway

  • Optic chiasma → Part of visual pathway

  • Lateral geniculate body (LGB) → Main thalamic relay for vision

  • Medial geniculate body (MGB) → Auditory pathway, not visual pathway

Exam pearl:
Vision → Lateral geniculate body; Hearing → Medial geniculate body.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ৫) Receptor organ in otolith organ is called.......?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The otolith organs are the utricle and saccule, and their sensory receptor organs are called maculae.

  • Macula → Receptor organ of utricle & saccule; detects linear acceleration and head position.

  • Cupula → Sensory structure associated with the crista ampullaris in semicircular canals.

  • Ampulla → Dilated portion of each semicircular canal containing the crista.

  • Labyrinth → The overall inner-ear structure containing vestibular and cochlear components.

Exam pearl:
Otolith organs (utricle + saccule) → Macula.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ৬) Which is not a pathological reflex?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The ciliospinal reflex is a normal superficial autonomic reflex, not a pathological reflex. It involves pupillary dilatation in response to painful stimulation of the skin of the neck.

Pathological reflexes include:

  • Babinski sign → indicates corticospinal tract/UMN dysfunction.

  • Clonus → indicates hyperreflexia, typically due to UMN lesions.

  • Pendular movements → may indicate cerebellar hypotonia.

Exam pearl:
Ciliospinal reflex = physiological reflex, not pathological.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ৭) Motion sickness is due to excessive and repeated stimulation of .......?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
Motion sickness (kinetosis) occurs mainly due to excessive/repeated stimulation of the vestibular apparatus, especially when there is a mismatch between visual input and vestibular signals.

  • Vestibular apparatus → detects movement and balance; excessive stimulation → motion sickness

  • Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, sweating

Exam pearl:
Motion sickness → excessive stimulation of the vestibular apparatus.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ৮) Which is a deep reflex?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
Supinator jerk (brachioradialis reflex) is a deep tendon reflex (DTR), elicited by tapping the brachioradialis tendon.

  • Supinator jerk → Deep reflex

  • Cremasteric reflex → Superficial reflex

  • Plantar reflex → Superficial reflex

  • Scapular reflex → Superficial reflex

Exam pearl:
Deep reflex → Supinator jerk (brachioradialis reflex).

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ৯) Which secondary vestibular fiber causes facilitation of muscle tone?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The vestibular reticular tract facilitates muscle tone, particularly by influencing the gamma motor system and extensor muscle activity. Vestibular inputs reach the reticular formation, which then modulates spinal motor neurons and helps maintain posture and muscle tone.

Other options:

  • Vestibulo-ocular tract: Coordinates eye movements with head movements; important for the vestibulo-ocular reflex.

  • Vestibulospinal tract: Directly influences spinal motor neurons and is important for postural control and extensor activity, but the question specifically asks for the secondary vestibular fiber causing facilitation of muscle tone, classically attributed to the vestibular reticular pathway.

  • Vestibulocerebellar tract: Carries vestibular information to the cerebellum for coordination and balance.

High-yield Vestibular recall:
Vestibular nuclei → reticular formation → vestibular reticular pathways → facilitation of muscle tone/postural reflexes.

Exam pearl:
Vestibular reticular tract = facilitates muscle tone and maintains posture.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১০) Which is a superficial reflex?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The plantar reflex is a superficial cutaneous reflex elicited by stroking the lateral border of the sole of the foot. The normal response is flexion of the toes.

Other options:

  • Ankle jerk: Deep tendon reflex (S1–S2).

  • Finger flexion reflex: Deep reflex, involving flexor muscles of the fingers.

  • Radial periosteal reflex: Deep tendon/periosteal reflex, mainly testing C5–C6.

High-yield Superficial reflexes recall:
Important superficial reflexes include plantar, abdominal, cremasteric, and anal reflexes.

Exam pearl:
Plantar reflex = superficial reflex; ankle jerk = deep reflex.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১১) What is the root value of Knee jerk?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The knee jerk (patellar reflex) is a deep tendon reflex mediated mainly by the femoral nerve. Its spinal root value is L2–L4, with L4 being the predominant root.

Other options:

  • L5–S2: Mainly involved in the ankle jerk and other lower-limb reflexes.

  • S3–S4: Associated with the anal reflex.

  • S4–S5: Mainly related to sacral/anal reflexes.

High-yield Reflex root values recall:

  • Biceps: C5–C6

  • Triceps: C7–C8

  • Knee jerk: L2–L4

  • Ankle jerk: S1–S2

Exam pearl:
Knee jerk → L2–L4 (mainly L4).

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১২) What will be the effect of lesion of right optic radiation?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The right optic radiation carries visual information from the left visual field of both eyes to the right visual cortex (occipital lobe). Therefore, a lesion of the right optic radiation causes left homonymous hemianopia.

Other options:

  • Right homonymous hemianopia: Caused by a lesion of the left optic tract/radiation/visual cortex.

  • Right nasal hemianopia: Not the typical defect from an optic radiation lesion.

  • Left nasal hemianopia: Not the typical defect from an optic radiation lesion.

High-yield Optic pathway recall:

Right visual field → left optic tract → left optic radiation → left visual cortex

Left visual field → right optic tract → right optic radiation → right visual cortex

Thus:
Right optic radiation lesion → Left homonymous hemianopia.

Exam pearl:

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১৩) What is the function of vestibulocerebellar tract?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The vestibulocerebellar tract carries vestibular information from the vestibular apparatus/nuclei to the flocculonodular lobe of the cerebellum. It helps maintain balance, equilibrium, posture, and coordination of movements, especially movements involving the head and eyes.

Other options:

  • Movements of eyeballs: Mainly mediated through vestibulo-ocular pathways.

  • Movements of head and body: Primarily related to vestibulospinal pathways and vestibular reflexes.

  • Facilitation of muscle tone: Mainly associated with vestibular reticular/vestibulospinal pathways.

High-yield Vestibular recall:

  • Vestibulocerebellar → coordination, equilibrium

  • Vestibulo-ocular → eye movements

  • Vestibulospinal → posture and head/body movements

  • Vestibular reticular → facilitation of muscle tone

Exam pearl:
Vestibulocerebellar tract = balance + coordination of movements.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১৪) Endolymph has large quantity of ....... ?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
Endolymph has a high concentration of K⁺ (potassium) and a low concentration of Na⁺, making its ionic composition similar to intracellular fluid. This high K⁺ concentration is essential for generating the endocochlear potential and facilitating sensory transduction by hair cells.

In contrast, perilymph has a high concentration of Na⁺ and low K⁺, resembling extracellular fluid.

Other options:

  • Sodium ions: Low in endolymph; high in perilymph.

  • Chlorine ions: Present but not the characteristic predominant cation.

  • Bicarbonate ions: Not the major distinguishing ion of endolymph.

High-yield Inner ear recall:
Endolymph → K⁺ rich, Na⁺ poor
Perilymph → Na⁺ rich, K⁺ poor

Exam pearl:
Endolymph = “K⁺ inside” → high potassium.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১৫) Lesion of left optic nerve leads to.......?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The left optic nerve carries all visual information from the left eye before the optic chiasm. Therefore, a complete lesion of the left optic nerve causes complete blindness (monocular blindness) of the left eye.

Other options:

  • Total blindness of right eye: Occurs with a complete lesion of the right optic nerve.

  • Binasal hemianopia: Rare; usually involves lesions affecting the uncrossed temporal retinal fibers of both optic nerves/chiasm.

  • Left homonymous hemianopia: Results from a lesion behind the optic chiasm on the right side, such as the right optic tract, optic radiation, or visual cortex.

High-yield Optic pathway recall:

  • Optic nerve lesion → ipsilateral monocular blindness

  • Optic chiasm lesion → bitemporal hemianopia

  • Optic tract/radiation/cortex lesion → contralateral homonymous hemianopia

Exam pearl:
Before the chiasm = same-eye loss; after the chiasm = opposite visual-field loss.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১৬) What is the root value of plantar response?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The plantar reflex is a superficial cutaneous reflex mediated mainly through the L5–S1/S2 spinal segments, with L5–S2 commonly given as its root value. The afferent limb travels via the tibial nerve, and the response is flexion of the toes in a normal adult.

Other options:

  • L4–S2: Too broad; L4 is not a principal root for the plantar reflex.

  • L4–S1: Includes L4 and omits S2.

  • S3–S4: More relevant to the anal reflex.

High-yield Reflex root values recall:

  • Knee jerk: L2–L4

  • Plantar reflex: L5–S2

  • Ankle jerk: S1–S2

  • Anal reflex: S3–S5

Exam pearl:
Plantar reflex → L5–S2; Babinski sign indicates an UMN lesion.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১৭) Reflex activities can be forcefully inhibited for some time but when the inhibition is suddenly removed, the reflex activity becomes more forceful than before inhibition. This is called......?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The rebound phenomenon occurs when a reflex activity is strongly inhibited for a period, and when the inhibition is suddenly removed, the reflex response becomes temporarily more vigorous than its original level. It reflects increased excitability of the reflex circuitry following release from inhibition.

Other options:

  • Fatigue: Progressive reduction in response following repeated or sustained stimulation.

  • Reciprocal inhibition: Inhibition of antagonist muscles when the agonist muscle is activated.

  • Spatial summation: Addition of postsynaptic potentials produced by simultaneous stimulation of multiple presynaptic inputs.

High-yield Reflex physiology recall:
Inhibition → sudden release → exaggerated reflex response = rebound phenomenon.

Exam pearl:
Rebound phenomenon = reflex “overshoot” after sudden removal of inhibition.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১৮) Second order neurons in visual pathway are ......?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
In the visual pathway, the neurons are classically arranged as:

  1. First-order neuron: Bipolar cells of the retina

  2. Second-order neuron: Ganglion cells of the retina

  3. Third-order neuron: Neurons of the lateral geniculate body (LGB)

  4. Optic radiation → primary visual cortex

The axons of retinal ganglion cells form the optic nerve, continue through the optic chiasm and optic tract, and mainly synapse in the lateral geniculate body.

Other options:

  • Bipolar cells: First-order neurons.

  • Lateral geniculate body: Contains third-order neurons of the main visual pathway.

  • Medial geniculate body: Part of the auditory pathway, not the visual pathway.

High-yield Visual pathway recall:
Bipolar → Ganglion → LGB → Visual cortex

Exam pearl:
2nd-order neuron of the visual pathway = retinal ganglion cell.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ১৯) What is the primary visual area number in cerebrum?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The primary visual cortex (V1) is located in Brodmann area 17, on the medial surface of the occipital lobe, mainly surrounding the calcarine sulcus.

Other options:

  • Area 16: Not the primary visual cortex.

  • Area 18: Visual association cortex (secondary visual area).

  • Area 19: Higher-order visual association cortex.

High-yield Cerebral cortex recall:

  • Brodmann area 17 → Primary visual cortex

  • Brodmann area 18 → Secondary visual association cortex

  • Brodmann area 19 → Visual association cortex

Exam pearl:
Area 17 = Primary visual; Areas 18 & 19 = Visual association.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ২০) What is the root value of Cremasteric reflex?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The cremasteric reflex is a superficial reflex mediated by L1–L2 spinal segments, with the genitofemoral nerve (L1–L2) carrying the afferent and efferent components. Stroking the medial thigh causes elevation of the ipsilateral testis through contraction of the cremaster muscle.

Other options:

  • T10–T12: Not the root value of the cremasteric reflex.

  • L2–L4: Mainly associated with the knee jerk.

  • L5–S2: Associated with the plantar reflex.

High-yield Reflex root values recall:

  • Cremasteric: L1–L2

  • Knee jerk: L2–L4

  • Plantar: L5–S2

  • Ankle jerk: S1–S2

Exam pearl:
Cremasteric reflex → L1–L2 → genitofemoral nerve.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ২১) Make it negative-interrogative: She cooks rice -
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The affirmative sentence “She cooks rice.” is in the simple present tense. To make it negative-interrogative, use:

Does + subject + not + base verb?

So:
She cooks rice. → Does she not cook rice?

After does, the main verb changes from cooks to the base form cook.

Other options:

  • Does she cook rice? — Interrogative, but not negative.

  • Has she not cooked rice? — Changes the tense to present perfect.

  • Does not she cook rice? — Incorrect word order in standard English.

High-yield Grammar recall:
Simple present negative-interrogative → Do/Does + subject + not + V₁?

Exam pearl:
She cooks → Does she not cook?

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ২২) If I had died! - Make it assertive -
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
“If I had died!” is an optative/exclamatory sentence expressing a wish about an unreal past situation. To make it assertive, use “I wish + past perfect”:

If I had died! → I wish I had died.

Other options:

  • I wish I were died: Grammatically incorrect; died cannot be used this way after were.

  • I wish I died: Simple past does not properly convey the unreal past situation intended here.

  • I wish I was dead: Grammatically possible in some contexts, but it changes the meaning from wishing that the past event of dying had occurred to wishing for a state of being dead.

High-yield Grammar recall:
For an unreal wish about the past:
I wish + subject + had + past participle (V³).

Exam pearl:
“If I had died!” → “I wish I had died.”

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ২৩) One should keep one’s promise. Choose the correct passive form -
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option1: One’s promise should be kept by him
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option3: One’s promise should be kept by one
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option4: One’s promise should be kept by himself
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The active sentence “One should keep one’s promise.” has the indefinite pronoun “one” as the subject. In the passive voice, it is natural and grammatically correct to omit the agent and write:

One should keep one’s promise → A promise should be kept.

The modal structure remains:

should + keep → should + be + kept

Other options:

  • One’s promise should be kept by him: “him” does not correctly refer back to the indefinite one.

  • One’s promise should be kept by one: Grammatically awkward and unnatural.

  • One’s promise should be kept by himself: “himself” has no appropriate masculine antecedent.

High-yield Grammar recall:
Modal passive:
Subject + modal + V₁ → Subject + modal + be + V³

Example:
You should obey the rules → The rules should be obeyed.

Exam pearl:
One should keep one’s promise → A promise should be kept.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ২৪) Choose the correct sentence:
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option1: This is the wisest plan of the two
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option2: This is the wiser plan of the two
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option3: This is the wiser plan between the two
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option4: This is the wisest plan among the two
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
When two persons or things are being compared, we use the comparative degree, not the superlative.

Therefore:

wiser → comparative → used for two
wisest → superlative → used for more than two

The standard construction is:

“the + comparative + of the two”

So, “This is the wiser plan of the two.” is correct.

Other options:

  • This is the wisest plan of the two: Incorrect because wisest is superlative and should not normally be used for only two.

  • This is the wiser plan between the two: Between is possible in some contexts, but “of the two” is the standard exam construction here.

  • This is the wisest plan among the two: Incorrect because wisest is inappropriate for two.

High-yield Grammar recall:
Two → comparative
More than two → superlative

Examples:

  • The better of the two

  • The best of the three

Exam pearl:
“Of the two” → use the comparative degree.

Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.question: ২৫) Which one is the correct sentence?
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option2: He is much well than bad
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option3: He is more good than bad
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.option4: He is most better than bad
Physiology + Sentences and Transformatio.exp:
The intended grammatical structure is “more good than bad”, where good and bad are being contrasted as complementary qualities.

Other options:

  • He is better than bad: Incorrect comparison because better is the comparative of good, while bad is being used as the contrasting quality.

  • He is much well than bad: Incorrect because well is an adverb/adjective of health and cannot be used here as good.

  • He is most better than bad: Incorrect because most better is a double comparative/superlative construction.

High-yield Grammar recall:
Good → better → best
Bad → worse → worst

Exam pearl:
For contrasting qualities in this construction: more good than bad.
